proposals.impact: Convert 4 stalled quiz sessions into starts
proposals.observation: All 4 quiz sessions in the 48-hour window loaded the intro screen and stopped. Zero starts. Zero completions. The furthest_step_distribution shows every single visitor stuck at intro_load. Two of those sessions came from a Google Docs viewer URL, which suggests someone previewed a shared document (likely a proposal or media kit) and tapped through to the quiz cold, with no warm context. The intro screen is doing nothing to earn the click.
proposals.proposal: The intro screen is losing every visitor before they answer a single question. The current text almost certainly opens with a generic promise rather than a specific, discomforting truth that makes a 28-year-old earning £65k feel named. Rewrite the intro headline and sub-copy to open on a concrete, specific tension Joel's ICP already lives with, so the cost of not starting feels higher than the cost of starting. No motivational framing. No promise of insight. Just the thing they recognise.
proposals.current_text:
Discover your money personality

Take our free quiz to understand your relationship with money and get personalised insights to help you build wealth.
proposals.new_text:
You earn well. So why does your bank account not show it?

This is a 3-minute quiz. It will not tell you to budget harder. It will show you the specific pattern that is quietly running your financial decisions — the one that explains why the spreadsheet never sticks, why you avoid opening that account, why "later" keeps arriving.

proposals.impact: Lift 37.5% open rate closer to Money Vigilance benchmark
proposals.observation: The Money Worship automation has a 37.5% open rate across 16 sends, the lowest of the three active sequences. Money Vigilance sits at 66.67% on 12 sends and Money Avoidance at 52.63% on 19 sends. The gap is not volume-related. Money Worship is structurally underperforming its sibling sequences, and the most controllable lever at this stage is the subject line, which determines whether the email gets opened before any copy does its work.
proposals.proposal: Rewrite the subject line of email 1 in the Money Worship sequence. The current subject line almost certainly leads with aspiration or achievement framing ("earn more", "want more", "money as success") which feels thin and generic to the ICP — people who already earn well and already know that wanting more money is not their actual problem. The replacement should name the specific discomfort Money Worship types live with: the feeling that their worth and their net worth are the same number.
proposals.current_text: subject: "Money and success: what your score really means"
proposals.new_text: subject: "When your salary drops, does your self-worth go with it?"

proposals.impact: Restore automated content pipeline before queue hits zero
proposals.observation: Two CI workflows failed on 12 September: "Daily Blog Post" at 07:55 and "Funnel-Hack Digest" at 12:22. The content queue currently shows 1 post queued and 47 published. With the Daily Blog Post workflow failing and only one item in the queue, the site is one successful run away from publishing nothing. A second failure tomorrow leaves the content calendar empty. Because .github/workflows/* is a blocked path for Fred, the fix here is to surface the failure clearly and give Joel the diagnostic he needs to resolve it himself before it compounds.
proposals.proposal: Add a visible workflow-failure notice to the repo README so Joel sees the broken pipeline the next time he opens the project, rather than discovering an empty blog two days from now. The README is not a blocked path. The notice should name both failed workflows, the timestamps, and the queue risk in plain terms so Joel can act without needing to read CI logs first.
